title: FoundationAD: guarded DC LDAPS cert-rotate (standby DC first, NTDS restart, :636 verify)
description: cert-rotate foundation-ad (GAP #9, v0.8.9) rotates each domain controller's LDAPS leaf, STANDBY DC FIRST then the PDC. Per DC: issue the leaf + build the PFX on vault-1 (openssl -- the Schannel-safe path), SFTP PFX + intermediate + root to the DC, import root->Root / intermediate->CA / leaf->My (all three load-bearing for the Schannel 36886 fix), verify the chain, Restart-Service NTDS + re-cycle ADWS in ONE SSH session (sshd is independent of NTDS so the session survives the ~20-30s restart -- no new SSH auth during the window, so the #10 self-fence can't occur), then verify the :636 handshake from the build host. If the standby DC's rotation fails, the PDC is left untouched. Live-verified 2026-07-07.

prerequisites.smokeGate: both DCs up with NTDS + Netlogon Running; vault-server PKI role allows dc-nexus + dc-nexus-2 (role-overlay-vault-pki-roles v3)

observe.what: the CURRENT LDAPS leaf serial on dc-nexus -- record it to compare after rotation
the per-DC old/new serial table: dc-nexus-2 (standby) rotates BEFORE dc-nexus (PDC); each new serial is what :636 now serves. The PDC is rotated LAST -- a failed standby rotation would skip it.

observe.where: ssh nexusadmin@192.168.70.1 'echo | openssl s_client -connect 192.168.70.240:636 -servername dc-nexus.nexus.lab 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -serial -issuer'
observe.what: dc-nexus:636 serves the NEW serial, issuer=CN=NexusPlatform Intermediate CA -- the LDAPS handshake completes with the rotated PKI cert

observe.where: ssh nexusadmin@192.168.70.240 'powershell -c "(Get-Service NTDS,Netlogon,ADWS).Status; Get-ADDomainController -Filter * | Select Name"'
observe.what: NTDS + Netlogon + ADWS Running and Get-AD* clean after the rotation -- AD auth was not interrupted (the NTDS restart stayed within the single session + ADWS was re-cycled)

whatProves: DC LDAPS cert rotation is a real, guarded, in-CLI operation (not an out-of-band overlay): standby-DC-first with abort-before-the-PDC, the NTDS restart is survived by keeping it in one SSH session, and LDAPS is proven to serve the new leaf on :636 -- without self-fencing the adapter's own SSH path or interrupting AD auth.
